page_data.en:
The South China Morning Post
July 12 1930
No. S. B. D. 1485.
Date 38 - 2 - 31
1917

SHANGHAI AND HONGKONG.

SOME COMPARISONS BETWEEN THE
NORTH AND SOUTH PORTS.

CABARETS AND GAMBLING.

(BY L. G. GRAHAM-TAYLOR.)

After living in Shanghai for the past ten years, the majestic beauty and hilly grandeur of Hongkong struck me much more forcibly yesterday than it did in 1918 when passing through for the first time. The Colony's beautiful beaches with the attendant sea bathing apparently more than compensate for the trying period encountered in the hot season when the intense humidity makes life extremely uncomfortable for all—especially for those who toil and live on the lower levels. Then, of course, the Colony has splendid and safe motor roads which lead to ideal spots. There is no motoring in Shanghai worthy of the name. People merely own motor cars for the convenience of getting to and from office and to transport themselves short distances at night.

In the past, one at least could take a drive round the Rubicon in the Jessfield district but now with armed robbers and murderers operating daily, one hesitates to travel even on the outside roads after dusk. Indeed, the Shanghai Municipal Council has warned residents on many occasions to refrain from motoring or walking in this area.

Early to Bed.

Then, one is told, Hongkong goes to bed before midnight. In Shanghai, the town is always awake. Cabarets make a point of advertising that they are "open all night." And they do very good business too, in spite of legislation. The decision that all bars, cabarets, dance halls, and places of entertainment must close at 2 a.m. from February 1 in the International Settlement was arrived at by the Municipal Council in December last after receiving reports from various departments. The recommendation to curtail the hours was endorsed by officials of the Municipal police and the view was expressed that most of the brawls and similar troubles occurred between 2 a.m. and daylight. Consequently, the new bye-law came into force but the result was that the cabaret business was transferred to the French Concession. In addition the Del Monte cabaret happens to be situated on a Municipal road but in Chinese territory so the new bye-law does not apply in this case and the cabaret seldom closes before 6 a.m.

The question of a clash of closing time regulations in adjoining settlements recalls the position which obtained in Tientsin some years ago. In the British Concession, all cabarets (there were about half a dozen) had to close at 1 a.m.

The principal cabaret was situated on the boundary of the British Concession and the ex-German Concession, which was under Chinese control. Within 30 yards of this cabaret and in the Chinese controlled area was another establishment owned by the same interests as the one on the border of the British Concession. There was no time limit in the Chinese controlled area—just a matter of a license. Accordingly, promptly at 1 a.m. the British Concession cabaret would close. The dancing partners, managers, orchestra, boys, etc., etc. would troop across the road to the establishment in the ex-German Concession and carry on until daylight. Patrons would follow, of course, and there was practically no interruption in the festivities. An almost identical situation obtains in Shanghai to-day except that it takes a few minutes more to transfer one's patronage to the "all-night" establishments.

Gambling Opportunities.

The new game of Hai-Alai has taken root in Shanghai and has become very popular with the Chinese. The game is played every night in the newly built Auditorium and a considerable amount of gambling takes place. There are also matinees on Sunday. As a matter of fact the game is very fascinating and apparently has come to stay. Greyhound racing may be seen four nights a week in spite of much protest on the part of the Chinese, and the courses are packed on all occasions. During 1929 there were something like 65 pony race meetings and this year the programme calls for about the same number distributed, of course, over the three courses. In addition there is motor-cycle dirt track racing which has met with some success as which has been handicapped by the heavy rains. There is also to be a "Velodrome" which will house cycle racing and one or two other sporting projects are in the course of formation. It will be seen, therefore, that Shanghai is doing its best to justify its overseas reputation of being the "Paris of the East."

Hongkong's Climate.

In discussing the attractions of Hongkong, the writer remembers that Hongkong people are very touchy on the subject. Some years ago, I think it was 1915, whilst traveling in the P. & O. s.s. Malwa, a fellow passenger, Engr. Commdr. James of "Taikoo" was very indignant one day when a friend suggested that Hongkong was "Hell upon Earth" during most months of the year. In answer to this slanderous and exaggerated statement, Commdr. James said that he had lived in the Colony for many years, I forget exactly how many he mentioned, and that both he and his family had found the climate excellent. In short he maintained that Hongkong was one of the best spots in the East. Whilst there can be no doubt that the spring months are delightful yet there also is no doubt that the summer months are exceptionally trying, although one hears less nowadays of mildewed shoes, musty clothing, etc., etc.

Shanghai's Offerings.

At the present time, the "Paris of the East" offers to the resident an opportunity to do business under the most disturbing conditions. And that is putting it mildly. The unprecedented position in exchange makes business practically an impossibility and many firms have had to reduce staff. Yet building continues. Never before has there been such a boom in land and property in Shanghai as at present. Land values have rapidly advanced to extraordinary levels and building is proceeding at increased speed in all sections of the International Settlement and French Concession. Almost daily one hears of further transactions in the real estate market, and architects and contractors are overwhelmed with work.

What precisely has caused this building boom is a debatable question but it is certain that the pouring into Shanghai of large quantities of money by powerful foreign interests has done much to restore the confidence lost in the turn of events and political uncertainties in Chinese quarters during the past few years. In addition, wealthy and influential Chinese have invested large sums in real estate engaging foreign companies to protect their interests and manage the properties.

The activity is not confined to one class of building. Although residential flats and apartment buildings predominate, large hotels, shops, houses, theatres, factories and godowns are in the course of construction.

《南华早报》
1930年7月12日
编号 S. B. D. 1485。
日期 38 - 2 - 31
1917

上海与香港。

南北两埠之若干比较。

歌舞厅与赌博。

（作者：L. G. GRAHAM-TAYLOR。）

在过去十年居住于上海之后，昨日香港那雄伟的秀丽景色与山峦的壮丽气势，比1918年我初次途经此地时更强烈地触动了我。该殖民地美丽的海滩以及随之而来的海水浴，显然足以弥补在炎热季节所遭遇的艰难时期，那时强烈的湿气使所有人的生活都极不舒适——尤其是对于那些在下层区域劳作和生活的人而言。当然，该殖民地拥有通往理想场所的优良且安全的机动车道。在上海，几乎谈不上有什么值得称道的驾车活动。人们拥有汽车仅仅是为了上下班方便，以及在夜间短途出行。

过去，人们至少可以在杰斯菲尔德区（Jessfield district，即兆丰公园一带）绕着“卢比孔河”（Rubicon，此处疑指某条道路或地标，原文如此）兜风，但现在由于武装抢劫犯和谋杀犯每日活动，人们甚至在黄昏后也不敢在外围道路上行驶。事实上，上海工部局已多次警告居民，避免在该区域驾车或步行。

早睡。

此外，有人告知，香港人在午夜前就寝。而在上海，这座城市始终处于清醒状态。歌舞厅特意宣传它们“通宵营业”。尽管有立法管制，它们的生意依然非常好。去年十二月，工部局在收到各部门报告后作出决定，自2月1日起，公共租界内所有酒吧、歌舞厅、舞厅及娱乐场所必须在凌晨2点关闭。缩减营业时间的建议得到了工部局警务处官员的支持，他们认为大多数斗殴及类似纠纷都发生在凌晨2点至天亮之间。因此，新的附例生效了，但结果是歌舞厅业务转移到了法租界。此外，德尔蒙特（Del Monte）歌舞厅恰好位于一条工部局道路上，但地处中国领土，因此新附例在此情况下不适用，该歌舞厅很少在早上6点前关门。

相邻租界在打烊时间规定上的冲突问题，让人想起几年前天津的情况。在英租界，所有歌舞厅（大约有五六家）必须在凌晨1点关闭。

主要的歌舞厅位于英租界与前德租界的边界上，后者当时由中国方面控制。在该歌舞厅30码以内、位于中国控制区内，有另一家由同一利益方拥有的场所。在中国控制区内没有时间限制——只需持有执照即可。因此，英租界的歌舞厅一到凌晨1点准时关闭。舞伴、经理、乐队、侍者等等人马便会穿过马路，前往位于前德租界的那家场所继续活动直到天亮。顾客自然也会跟随，庆祝活动实际上并未中断。如今上海的情况几乎完全相同，只不过将光顾转移到那些“通宵”场所需要多花几分钟时间。

赌博机会。

一种名为“海阿莱”（Hai-Alai，音译，可能指回力球 Jai-Alai）的新游戏已在上海扎根，并深受中国人欢迎。每晚在新建的大礼堂（Auditorium）进行该游戏，其间伴随着大量的赌博活动。周日还有日场表演。事实上，这项运动非常迷人，看来已站稳脚跟。尽管遭到中国人的强烈抗议，每周仍有四个晚上可以观看赛狗，且每次赛场都挤满了人。1929年间，小型马赛（pony race）约有65次，今年的赛程安排也大致相同，当然分布在三个赛马场进行。此外，还有摩托车泥地赛道比赛，取得了一定的成功，尽管受到了大雨的不利影响。还将建造一个“自行车赛车场”（Velodrome），用于举办自行车比赛，另外还有一两个其他体育项目正在筹划中。由此可见，上海正尽其所能，以不负其作为“东方巴黎”的海外声誉。

香港的气候。

在讨论香港的吸引力时，笔者记得香港人对这个话题非常敏感。几年前，我想是1915年，当我乘坐半岛与东方轮船公司（P. & O.）的“马尔瓦号”（Malwa）轮船旅行时，一位同船乘客、“太古”（Taikoo）公司的工程师指挥官詹姆斯（Engr. Commdr. James）有一天非常愤怒，因为一位朋友暗示香港在一年中的大多数月份里都是“人间地狱”。针对这一诽谤且夸张的说法，詹姆斯指挥官回答说，他已在该殖民地生活多年，我忘记了他具体提到是多少年，他和他的家人都觉得气候极佳。简而言之，他坚持认为香港是东方最好的地方之一。虽然毫无疑问春季月份令人愉悦，但同样毫无疑问的是，夏季月份格外难熬，尽管如今较少听到关于鞋子发霉、衣物霉变等等的抱怨了。

上海的供给。

目前，“东方巴黎”为居民提供了一个在最令人不安的条件下经商的机会。这话说得还算含蓄。汇率的前所未有的状况使得商业活动几乎成为不可能，许多商行不得不裁员。然而，建筑施工仍在继续。上海的土地和房地产繁荣程度从未像现在这样高涨。地价迅速攀升至惊人的水平，公共租界和法租界各区域的建筑速度都在加快。人们几乎每天都能听到房地产市场的进一步交易消息，建筑师和承包商们忙得不可开交。

究竟是什么导致了这场建筑热潮，这是一个有争议的问题，但可以肯定的是，强大的外国势力向上海涌入大量资金，极大地恢复了因过去几年中国方面的局势变化和政治不确定性而丧失的信心。此外，富有且有影响力的中国人在房地产上投入了巨额资金，聘请外国公司来保护他们的利益并管理物业。

这种活动并不局限于某一类建筑。虽然住宅公寓和公寓楼占主导地位，但大型酒店、商店、房屋、剧院、工厂和仓库也在建设中。

S. B. D 1485

Going back to the early history
of property in Shanghai or to the
time when Shanghai was first made
an open port, land was obtainable
at agricultural prices. Records
are in existence of land purchased
at $150 per mow. Contrast this
with the price of $600,000 per
mow which is about the value of
land situated at the junction of
Nanking Road and the Bund. Some
amazing statistics are available in
connexion with land values.
Eight hundred million taels is the
estimated market value of land
under foreign registration in the
International Settlement and in
the case of land in some parts of
the Western district it is estim-
ated that the value is fifteen times
greater than the value placed upon
it 20 years ago. In 1855 there
were merely 187 registered lots as
against over 10,000 registered
British lots to-day.
Returning again to the matter
of general business in Shanghai,
the disturbing influence of con-
tinued and useless civil war also
makes business hazardous if not
impossible in many areas which,
in normal times, were large buyers
and sellers of produce.
Prohibitive Rentals.
Shanghai also offers at the pre-
sent time a house or flat at a pro-
hibitive rental out of all propor-
tion to its real worth and it will
also sell you the necessities of
life at a price. This price will be
almost double that paid a year ago.
In other words the cost of living
has gone up practically 100 per
cent. within the past twelve
months. Some firms granted in-
creases to their employees but the
majority have not. Mainly be-
cause they cannot. Business would
not justify such extra expenditure.
Accordingly most people find it
exceedingly difficult to make both
ends meet. Home leave is prac-
tically out of the question for all
and it is interesting to note that at
the present rate of exchange a
passage to London costs about
$2,000. The writer leaves it to
the reader to calculate what it
costs for a man, wife, and family
to travel nowadays.
The Visitor in Shanghai.
To the visitor, Shanghai offers
excellent hotel accommodation at
rates which compare with most in
the East although it is within the
knowledge of the writer that a
certain foreign nobleman—chair-
man of a League of Nation's Com-
mittee—who recently passed
through Shanghai in connexion
with a commission of inquiry
found the rates prohibitive at a
certain hotel and sought accommo-
dation elsewhere within a few
hours of his arrival.
Shanghai also offers a night
life second to none and compar-
able with anything encountered in
the world. One, if one so desires,
need never go to bed for the
customary period. There is
always somewhere to go. Although
the following obviously is not the
usual routine followed by the
majority of visitors, nevertheless,
it was the programme followed
with certain minor alterations
for some days by an acquaintance
of the writer recently:

11 a.m. Breakfast consisting of
an egg nog (very cold) and
another egg nog.
11.30 a.m. to 12.15 p.m. Bath
and some reflection on last
night's doings.
12.30 p.m. Club
1.30 p.m. to 2.30. Lunch
2.30 p.m. to 4 p.m. Visiting
local agents.
4.15 p.m. to 8.30 p.m. Bridge at
the Club.
8.30 p.m. and onwards. Dinner
out; several cabarets, even-
tually arriving at hotel be-
tween 6 a.m. and 7.30 a.m.
tired but not too unhappy.
It may come as a surprise to
many but it is a fact that statis-
tics show that the bulk of the
money spent in Shanghai's
cabarets comes out of the purse
of visitors.
From 8 p.m. onwards one may
always vary the routine by calling
in at the Greyhound tracks or the
Hai-Alai Auditorium. A gamble
on any scale is always available
at either of these.
Shanghai's Noises.
In addition to all these experi-
ences, the visitor will be able to
share with the resident the ap-
palling and nerve-racking noises
in the streets of Shanghai, the
existence of which has just been
brought to the notice of the city
fathers after almost a year of con-
tinuous correspondence in the
press.
Really and truly the noise in
Shanghai to-day is something
frightful. I think there are some-
thing slightly under 9,000 motor
vehicles licensed and as all of
these have to operate on roads
within an area of something like
seven miles square, some idea of
the din can, perhaps, be imagined.
Chinese owned cars are the
worst offenders with hire cars
coming a close second. Then we
have the buses and the trams.
The former are not too bad but
the drivers of the latter—particu-
larly in the French Concession—
play a tattoo on the gong for
stretches of several hundred
yards in the main thoroughfares.
And, it must be borne in mind
with the night life of Shanghai
ever on the increase, motor cars are
never off the streets. Greyhound
racing and Hai-Alai never finish
before 12.30 a.m. and often as
late as 1.30 a.m. At this hour,
therefore, some 10,000 people have
to be transported to their homes
or elsewhere.
So it must be conceded by all
that your Colony is by far the best
off. You have the sea, early
hours, the British Government,
and a rattling good cricket team.
What could be nicer?

（批：JWM / hls）

回顾上海的地产早期历史，或者追溯到上海最初开埠的时期，土地可以以农业用地的价格获得。现存记录显示，当时购买土地的价格为每亩150元。相比之下，位于南京路与外滩交汇处的土地价值约为每亩60万元。关于地价，有一些令人震惊的统计数据可供参考。在国际租界内，以外商名义登记的土地估计市场价值为八亿两白银；而在西区某些地段，据估计其价值是20年前估值的十五倍。1855年，注册地块仅有187块，而如今注册的英商地块已超过10,000块。

再回到上海的一般商业事务上来，持续且无益的内战所造成的动荡影响，使得在许多地区开展业务变得充满风险，甚至不可能进行，而这些地区在正常时期本是农产品的大宗买卖市场。

高昂的租金。
目前，上海提供的房屋或公寓租金高得令人望而却步，与其实际价值完全不成比例；此外，这里的生活必需品售价也极高。这一价格几乎是一年前支付价格的两倍。换言之，在过去十二个月里，生活成本实际上上涨了100%。有些公司给员工增加了薪水，但大多数公司没有这样做。这主要是因为它们无力承担。商业状况无法证明此类额外支出是合理的。因此，大多数人发现收支平衡极其困难。对于所有人来说，回国休假实际上已不可能；值得注意的是，按目前的汇率计算，前往伦敦的船票费用约为2,000元。作者留给读者去计算，如今一个人带着妻子和孩子旅行需要花费多少。

上海的访客。
对于访客而言，上海提供优质的酒店住宿，其费率与东方大多数地方相当，尽管据作者所知，某位外国贵族——国际联盟某委员会主席——最近因调查委员会事务途经上海时，发现某家酒店的费率高得令人望而却步，因此在抵达后几小时内便另寻住处。

上海的夜生活也是首屈一指，可与世界上任何地方的夜生活相媲美。如果愿意，人们完全可以不按常规时间就寝。总有地方可去。虽然以下安排显然不是大多数访客通常遵循的例行程序，但作者的一位熟人最近在几天内确实大致按照此计划行事，仅做了少许改动：

上午11点：早餐，包括一杯蛋奶酒（非常冰）和另一杯蛋奶酒。
上午11:30至中午12:15：沐浴，并回味昨晚的活动。
中午12:30：俱乐部
下午1:30至2:30：午餐
下午2:30至4:00：拜访当地代理商。
下午4:15至晚上8:30：在俱乐部打桥牌。
晚上8:30及之后：外出晚餐；光顾几家歌舞厅，最终在早上6点至7:30之间回到酒店，虽感疲惫，但心情尚佳。

这可能令许多人感到惊讶，但统计数据显示，在上海歌舞厅花费的大部分资金确实来自访客的腰包，这是一个事实。

从晚上8点开始，人们总是可以通过去赛狗场或海光电影院（Hai-Alai Auditorium）来改变日常行程。在这两个地方，随时都可以进行各种规模的赌博。

上海的噪音。
除了上述所有体验外，访客还能与居民共同承受上海街道上那些可怕且令人神经紧张的噪音。经过报刊上近一年的连续通信讨论，这些噪音的存在刚刚引起市政当局的注意。

说实在的，如今上海的噪音确实可怕。我想，持有执照的机动车辆略少于9,000辆，由于所有这些车辆都必须在一个约七平方英里的区域内道路上行驶，或许可以想象出那种喧嚣的程度。

华人拥有的汽车是噪音最大的肇事者，出租轿车紧随其后。此外还有公共汽车和有轨电车。前者情况还不算太糟，但后者——特别是在法租界——的司机在主要干道上长达数百码的路段内不停地敲击铃铛。而且，必须考虑到，随着上海夜生活的日益丰富，汽车从未离开过街道。赛狗活动和海光电影院（Hai-Alai）的结束时间从不早于凌晨12:30，经常晚至凌晨1:30。因此，在这个时间点，约有10,000人需要被运送回家或前往其他地方。

因此，所有人都必须承认，你们的殖民地处境要好得多。你们拥有海洋、规律的作息时间、英国政府，以及一支非常出色的板球队。还有什么比这更美好的呢？

（批：JWM / hls）
（批：呈报。（总巡捕房及特别分支）情报）
（批：归档文件 Who 18.30 / S.2. / NK / 1930年9月21日）
